source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1.  Flash BMC Firmware :
        Follow the standard procedure to perform the first BMC firmware flash.
        Ensure you follow the official firmware update guidelines during this process.

    2.  Second BMC Firmware Update :
        Begin the second BMC firmware update.
        At some point during the update process,  AC power to the server to simulate an unexpected power interruption.

    3. Expected Outcome:
        After the server is powered off, reconnect the AC power.
        The system should automatically detect the simulated BMC firmware crash and initiate recovery.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. The BMC firmware should automatically revert to the previous stable version, which was the state after the initial BMC firmware flash.
2. The server should boot normally, and the BMC firmware should return to normal operation.

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: BMC firmware images + human AC power control + BMC recovery procedure
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Crash BMC and recovery: crash-and-recover the BMC by cutting AC power mid-firmware-update to simulate a crash, then verifying the BMC auto-reverts to the previous stable firmware. Requires a person to physically cut/restore AC power and an operator to drive the two BMC firmware flashes; the agent cannot simulate the power interruption nor boot the BMC flash recovery console.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: operator performs the two firmware flashes with the intentional AC cut at the second update, re-applies AC and records the revert to the previous firmware + normal BMC boot; agent cannot produce this evidence.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: crashing the BMC mid-flash and AC-cycling is physically destructive to the BMC firmware state; human-only, perform carefully on a test unit.

historical_reviews.deepseek: NO; correctly identifies human AC interruption and destructive firmware risk.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: PACKAGE / IMPROVED; treats the manual AC cut as attended setup rather than the core fault injection.
historical_reviews.round_02: YES; entry 742/2291 covers the exact variant.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: No V3/V3.1 record exists for this variant.

original_test_intent: Prove BMC dual-image or recovery logic by establishing a known-good image, interrupting a second BMC flash through AC removal, restoring AC and confirming rollback plus normal host/BMC recovery.
original_method: Two firmware flashes with a human-timed AC power interruption during the second update, followed by reconnection and manual/system recovery evidence.
manual_activity: An engineer must perform and witness the intentional AC removal/restoration at the approved update phase. That physical destructive fault is the core stimulus, so the case is MANUAL ONLY.
required_inputs: Compatible signed BMC image pair and hashes
Isolated unit, physical AC control and independent console
safety_requirements: One authorized approval may cover the unchanged destructive plan; verify isolated target, stable baseline and independent recovery first.
Do not substitute software reboot/BMC power-off for the source AC interruption without a project override that explicitly changes method/coverage.
Never interrupt at an unapproved phase, automatically retry, reverse an uncertain flash or hide the first failure.
Stop on loss of recovery access, unexpected bank state, smoke/thermal/electrical hazard or ambiguous target identity.
agent_execution_scope: Prepare the approved plan, verify packages, collect flash/task/console/power/version/SEL evidence and analyze rollback/boot health.
Do not perform or claim the physical AC operation or final verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve and execute the timed physical AC interruption/restoration.
Own recovery decisions and final verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Its narrative correctly preserves the human AC boundary but supplies no executable command, matching the physical nature of the case.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use the platform's approved flash and recovery SOP; instrument task phase and power timeline without replacing the physical fault.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Two flashes, AC interruption/reconnection, prior-version rollback and 10/10-minute values remain.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Record bank/version baseline, execute the two approved flashes, have an engineer remove AC at the vendor-defined phase, restore AC once, and correlate power, recovery-bank, version, console, SEL and host-health timelines.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only a BMC design with documented interrupted-update recovery.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC bootloader/recovery/firmware and updater versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Vendor BMC update interruption and recovery SOP.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact trigger, bank evidence and stop/recovery gates while preserving the physical fault.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; makes rollback attribution auditable.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Vendor recovery contract and isolated hardware.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: May permanently remove management access or prevent boot.

project_override_considerations: A PDU may be used only if the approved project method defines it as real AC removal at the SUT and documents equivalent coverage; a BMC command or software reboot is not equivalent. Seq 182 is not generalized, but this row independently requires physical AC interruption by its own source.
expected_evidence: Approved destructive plan and isolated SUT identity
Image hashes, bank/version baseline and first-flash success
Second-update task phase plus manual AC-off/on timeline

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The phrase omits the verb before `AC power`, but the surrounding text, criteria and same-row review unambiguously specify an AC interruption and rollback recovery test.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The case is dangerous and input-dependent but its intent is clear. With approved hardware/SOP it is executable by an engineer, so MANUAL ONLY is appropriate rather than BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Agrees on the physical human boundary and adds structured evidence controls.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Corrects PACKAGE to MANUAL ONLY because the physical AC fault is the core test stimulus, not setup preceding an automated core.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Keeps engineer verdict separate and avoids globalizing the Seq 182 case decision.

review_improvement: Defines bank/version attribution, interruption trigger, independent recovery and no-retry safety gates.
independent_technical_reasoning: The recovery property is only exercised by a deliberately timed loss of AC during a BMC write. Although software can monitor and collect evidence, the essential physical fault must be performed by an engineer and cannot be claimed by the agent.
